rv.q: The revival of DANCE at the Los Angeles Theatre Center – a co-production by Artists at Play and the Latino Theatre Company – is an artful rendering of an infrequently-staged Hwang work.
That it raises our consciousness with as much vibrancy as historical accuracy only adds to its appeal.
Overall, this was an interesting and enlightening show well presented by all.
It is an affirming, meditative, and haunting experience to watch these two men discover the vulnerabilities of a seemingly immovable object while they chip away at it.

cn.t: Critics praise this spare, dignified revival of Hwang's 1981 play about Chinese railroad workers, highlighting striking performances and the poignant blend of historical drama with Chinese Opera that explores identity and defiance.
